title: Control console
subtitle: Configure who gets in and what they can administer: onboard users, connect SSO, and shape workspaces and agent-groups.

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.caption: Create and manage programmatic credentials for CI/CD pipelines, Terraform providers, and other integrations.
apiKeys.createHint: The key value will be shown once after creation. Store it securely.
apiKeys.noneHint: Create an API key to enable programmatic access to this deployment.
apiKeys.revokeBody: Revoke the API key "{{name}}"? This action is permanent and will immediately invalidate all requests using this key.
apiKeys.rotateBody: Rotate the API key "{{name}}"? The old key will be revoked immediately and a new key will be generated.
apiKeys.revealHint: Copy this key now. It will not be shown again.
apiKeys.revealWarning: This is the only time the full key value is displayed. Store it in a secure location.
apiKeys.scopeHint: A tenant-bound key acts only within the current tenant. A superadmin key is cross-tenant.
apiKeys.truncatedHint: There are more API tokens than shown; this page takes rows by id — assigned at creation — so later rows are missing. These are LIVE credentials: a token you cannot see here still authenticates, and you cannot revoke it from this screen. A key not listed does not demonstrate that it does not exist.

license.title: Edition & license
license.caption: Install and manage the commercial license. Changes apply live — no restart. Upgrading from community to business is a one-time binary swap; the license itself is hot-applied on the same installation, with no data loss.
license.superadminOnly: Only a superadmin can view or change the license.
license.communityNote: This is the community edition. The license is verified and displayed but does not change this build's behavior. User accounts are unlimited in every self-hosted edition — the license never caps them; the business build adds the commercial add-ons. Install it here, then swap to the business binary (one restart) to upgrade in place.
license.expiredBanner: This commercial license has expired: the enterprise add-ons are inactive and the deployment behaves as the community edition. Your data and your user accounts are intact — no account was capped, disabled or deleted. Install a renewed license to restore the add-ons.
license.managedExternally: The license is managed out-of-band (source: {{source}}). Edit that source to change it — installing from the console is disabled to avoid a shadowed file.
license.installHint: Paste the signed license blob, or upload the license file. It is verified against this build's key before it is stored, then applied live.
license.downgradeWarn: The engine asked for an explicit confirmation before applying this change. Existing accounts are never deleted and user accounts are never capped. Confirm to proceed.
license.removeBody: This removes the license for {{licensee}} and reverts to the community edition. Your data is intact; existing accounts are never deleted.
license.removeBodyGeneric: This removes the installed license and reverts to the community edition. Your data is intact; existing accounts are never deleted.
license.removed: License removed; reverted to the community edition.

people.title: Users
people.caption: Onboard a person into this organization with an admin-set password or an email invitation. SSO users are provisioned automatically on first login.
people.pendingCaption: Invitations awaiting acceptance. The single-use link sets the password and activates the account.
people.revokeBody: The invitation link for {{email}} will stop working immediately.

members.title: Active members
members.caption: Tenant roster from SCIM and console onboarding. Shows roles, groups, status and whether sign-in is SSO-only.
members.readOnlyNotice: You need user read access to view active members.
members.noneHint: Members appear here after onboarding, SCIM provisioning or first SSO login.
members.externalManagedNotice: IdP-provisioned accounts can be reconciled back by the identity provider after a local enable or disable.
members.idpManagedConfirm: This account is provisioned by an IdP. The IdP may reconcile the active state back on its next sync.
members.disableBody: {{email}} will be deactivated through SCIM. The account is not deleted.

superadmins.title: Superadmins
superadmins.caption: Enable or disable the internal superadmin accounts. Disabling is reversible and non-destructive — the account is marked inactive and its sessions and tokens are revoked, never deleted. The last active superadmin cannot be disabled.
superadmins.enableBody: {{email}} will be able to sign in again. Previously revoked sessions and tokens are not restored.
superadmins.disableBody: {{email}} will be signed out and its sessions and API tokens revoked. The account is not deleted and can be re-enabled. Another active superadmin must remain.

onboard.title: Onboard user
onboard.body: Create or add an account to this organization. A new account is never a superadmin, and the role can never exceed your own.
onboard.displayNameHint: A human label shown in the console.
onboard.emailHint: The login identifier. SSO users sign in through the IdP instead.
onboard.roleHint: The built-in role granted in this organization.
onboard.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. The user can change it later.
onboard.inviteCreatedBody: Share this single-use link with {{email}} — it is shown once. Email delivery, when configured, also sends it.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.caption: Connect your identity provider (OIDC or SAML). Secrets are encrypted at rest and never shown again. Configuring SSO is a deployment-wide, superadmin-only, step-up-protected action.
sso.superadminOnly: SSO is a deployment-wide setting; only a superadmin can view or change it.
sso.builderUnavailable: This build can store SSO configuration but cannot activate it. Rebuild with the enterprise tag to enable OIDC/SAML login.
sso.redirectUriHint: Register this exact URL at your IdP.
sso.secretSet: A secret is stored (fingerprint {{hint}}). Leave blank to keep it.
sso.emailAttrHint: Optional. Defaults to common attribute names.
sso.spSignCertHint: Optional. Signs AuthnRequests and is published in the SP metadata as the use="signing" key (RSA or EC; the encryption keypair above must be RSA). Leave both boxes blank to keep the stored keypair. When you set one half, set the other: a keypair with only one half cannot be loaded and stops SSO logins for this provider.
sso.keySet: A key is stored (fingerprint {{hint}}). Leave blank to keep it.
sso.deleteBody: SSO login will stop working and revert to local credentials. The stored secrets are deleted.

enforcement.title: Login enforcement
enforcement.caption: Optional deny-closed controls over how users sign in. Configured here; enforced by the business build.
enforcement.requireSsoHint: Blocks password login while an identity provider is active, so an absent or disabled IdP can never lock everyone out. The business build enforces it; an operator kill-switch is the break-glass.
enforcement.networkAllowlistHint: One CIDR per line (e.g. 10.0.0.0/8 or 2001:db8::/32). When set, logins are accepted only from these ranges; empty means no IP restriction. It guards the login surface (password and SSO completion) using the real connection IP, not a forwarded header — it is not a network firewall.
enforcement.enforcedUnavailable: Stored, not enforced by this build
enforcement.unavailableBanner: This build stores the enforcement posture but does not enforce it. Rebuild with the enterprise tag to enforce require-SSO and the network allow-list — it never silently enforces or fakes the control.
enforcement.outOfScopeBanner: This build enforces login policy, but only over the deployment-wide primary identity provider. The posture stored here is not the one it reads, so it is not applied. Set it on the deployment-wide primary to have it take effect.
enforcement.noIdpWarning: Require-SSO takes effect only once an identity provider is enabled above (anti-lockout).

sso.groupsClaimHint: Optional. The ID-token/UserInfo claim carrying the user's groups (e.g. "groups"). The business build maps them to roles at login.
sso.groupsAttrHint: Optional. The multi-valued SAML attribute carrying the user's groups (e.g. "memberOf"). The business build maps them to roles at login.

groups.title: Group mapping & provisioning
groups.caption: How directory groups from the IdP become roles, and whether SCIM is the sole authority for accounts. Configured here; mapped by the business build.
groups.scimAuthoritativeHint: When on, an SSO login never creates an account or changes group membership — SCIM owns the directory. When off, first login provisions the user and adds (never removes) the groups the IdP asserts.
groups.unavailableBanner: This build extracts groups from the assertion but does not map them to roles. The business build turns asserted groups into grants at login.

scope.label: Scope
scope.globalHint: The default IdP used by every tenant that has no IdP of its own.
scope.tenantHint: This tenant's own IdP. It only takes effect at login in the business build (the multi-IdP capability); activating a second IdP requires it.

idp.label: Identity provider
idp.hint: A scope can federate several identity providers. Home-realm routing by email domain is configured below. Only a tenant scope can run several active providers at once — each extra one must claim its own domains, and your licence may still refuse it; the deployment-wide scope activates only the primary. The open build resolves the deployment-wide primary and nothing else.
idp.addBody: Give the new IdP a short alias. It identifies this IdP within the scope and is its login routing key.
idp.aliasHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (e.g. "okta", "azure-ad"). 1–31 characters.

domains.title: Home-realm routing
domains.caption: Route a login to this IdP by the user's email domain.
domains.label: Claimed email domains
domains.hint: One domain per line (e.g. corp.com). Each domain is globally unique across IdPs; an email-first login for that domain routes here.
domains.unavailableBanner: Domains are stored but this build does not route by them; home-realm routing requires the business edition.

secrets.title: Secret store
secrets.caption: Named secrets in the deployment-wide sealed store. Reference one from a connector config as store:<name>; the value is resolved at connection time, so you reconfigure without restarting. The value is never shown — only a short fingerprint confirms a secret is set or changed.
secrets.superadminOnly: The secret store is a deployment-wide setting; only a superadmin can view or change it.
secrets.sealerUnavailable: This build can list secrets but has no sealer wired, so values cannot be stored. Configure a sealer backend to enable the store.
secrets.noneHint: Add a secret to reference it from a connector config as store:<name>.
secrets.name: Name
secrets.nameHint: A handle like gdrive/token. Letters, digits, dot, underscore, dash and slash. Immutable once set.
secrets.valueHint: The secret value. It is sealed on save and never shown again.
secrets.valueSet: A value is stored (fingerprint {{hint}}). Leave blank to keep it; enter a new value to rotate.
secrets.deleteBody: The secret is removed from the store. Any connector config that references store:<name> will fail to resolve until you recreate it.

connectors.title: Connectors
connectors.caption: Add and configure the connectors the engine ingests from, with their credentials sealed at rest. A change is applied to the running engine without a restart. Deployment-wide, superadmin-only and step-up protected.
connectors.superadminOnly: Connectors are a deployment-wide setting; only a superadmin can view or change them.
connectors.unavailable: This build did not wire connector onboarding; connectors are configured from the boot file instead.
connectors.noneHint: Add a connector to start ingesting from a system.
connectors.kindHint: The system this connector reads from.
connectors.name: Name
connectors.tenantHint: The business tenant its observations belong to.
connectors.pollSecondsHint: 0 runs once or streams; a positive value re-runs a batch source on that interval.
connectors.modeHint: export reads an offline/exported view; live reads the upstream system live. An unset mode is treated as export.
connectors.secretSet: A credential is stored. Leave blank to keep it.
connectors.pluginNote: This connector runs out-of-process; its fields are not known to the console. Configure it with the settings below. It is validated when you save.
connectors.testUnavailable: Test is available only for in-process connectors; this one is validated when you save.
connectors.savedNotApplied: Connector saved, but not applied live: {{note}}
connectors.deleteBody: The connector stops ingesting and its sealed credentials are deleted.
connectors.assignmentsDesc: Assign global connectors to workspaces. Once a connector has assignments, it is visible only in those workspaces.
connectors.assignmentsForbidden: You need connector-assignment read access to view assignments.
connectors.noAssignmentsDesc: Global connectors with no assignments are visible in every workspace.
connectors.assignConnectorDesc: Choose a global connector and the workspace to assign it to.
connectors.workspaceConnectorsDesc: Connectors created for and confined to a specific workspace.
connectors.wsConnectorsForbidden: You need workspace-connector read access to view workspace connectors.
connectors.noWsConnectorsDesc: Create a connector confined to a workspace with its own credentials.
connectors.deleteWsConnectorDesc: Delete {{name}} from {{workspace}}? This removes its workspace-owned credentials.
connectors.createWsConnectorDesc: Create a connector confined to a workspace with its own credentials.
connectors.configHint: One non-secret key=value setting per line.
connectors.secretsHint: One key=value per line. On edit, leave a value blank to keep the stored secret reference.

reload.confirmTitle: Reload runtime and reconcile the source roster?
reload.confirmBody: Reloads the live source roster and re-resolves the license. Boot-time configuration is left untouched — a restart is still needed for it.
reload.confirmDisrupt: Every source connection is re-established: removed and rotated sources are torn down live before the roster is re-applied, interrupting any ingestion in flight.
reload.toastClean: Runtime reloaded. Some boot-time settings still need a restart to take effect.
reload.toastPartial: Runtime reloaded in part — some sources were rejected. See the report.
reload.reportCaption: The outcome of reconciling the live source roster and the license.
reload.partialBody: The reload finished, but the engine rejected these sources and left them unchanged:
reload.restartBody: These configuration domains are read once at boot and are NOT applied by this reload. A restart is required for them to take effect:

catalog.caption: Every connector this build can wire, read from the engine — {{count}} in total. Browsing is read-only; adding one still requires a step-up.
catalog.title: Supported connectors

hosting.self_hostedHint: You run this system yourself — the connector’s declared endpoint defaults to this machine.
hosting.unknownHint: This connector declares no endpoint, so where it runs was not determined. It does NOT mean vendor-hosted.
hosting.vendor_hostedHint: A provider-operated API — the connector’s declared endpoint defaults to the vendor’s URL.

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.caption: Soft-isolation containers within this organization. Scope admins, agents and resources to a workspace. Creating one is owner-only; archived workspaces keep their history.
workspaces.renameBody: Change the workspace display name. The slug and audit history stay unchanged.
workspaces.name: Name
workspaces.slugHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Immutable once set.
workspaces.archiveBody: An archived workspace is kept for reference but not offered for new scoping. Its agents and resources are not deleted.
workspaces.ownerOnly: Only the organization owner can create workspaces.

agents.readOnlyNotice: You need agent read access to view agents.
agents.title: Agents
agents.caption: Register and maintain the individual agents governed by this tenant.
agents.formCaption: Define the agent identity, runtime kind, workspace scope and optional JSON attributes.
agents.name: Name
agents.jsonObjectError: Labels and metadata must be valid JSON objects.
agents.noneHint: Create an agent to scope access, policy and audit records to an individual runtime.
agents.deactivateBody: Deactivate {{name}}? The agent remains in history but is no longer active.
agents.deleteBody: Delete {{name}}? This removes the agent record. Audit history remains immutable.
agents.truncatedHint: There are more registered agents than shown; this page takes rows by id. An agent not listed here does not demonstrate that it is unregistered.
agents.workspacesTruncatedHint: More workspaces exist than were loaded. One beyond this page shows as a raw id in the table and cannot be picked when creating or editing an agent — the truncation blocks an operation, it does not merely hide a row.

groups.title: Agent-groups
groups.caption: Named collections of agents the access engine targets with a single grant.
groups.readOnlyNotice: You need agent read access to view agent-groups.
groups.name: Name
groups.slugImmutable: The slug is the stable scope handle and cannot be changed.
groups.workspaceImmutable: Workspace scope is set when the group is created.
groups.membersCaption: Add or remove agents from this group by agent ID.
groups.agentIdHint: Paste the ID of an existing agent in this tenant.
groups.membersNoneHint: Add an agent ID to make it part of this group.
groups.deleteBody: The group and its membership are removed. The member agents are not deleted.

roles.readOnlyNotice: You need governance RBAC access to manage roles and delegation.

authority.title: Your delegation authority
authority.superadmin: You are a superadmin — you can delegate any role within any scope.
authority.none: You have no delegation authority in this organization. An owner or admin must grant you a scoped-admin role first.
authority.caption: You can only delegate within these scopes, and never more than these permissions. The engine re-checks every change.
authority.loadError: Could not load your delegation authority. Try again.

grants.title: Scoped grants
grants.caption: Assign a role to a user or a built-in role within a scope — this is how you make someone a workspace admin or a resource-class admin.
grants.subject: Subject
grants.revokeBody: The subject loses this scoped role immediately. Revoking is itself ceiling-checked.

grantForm.title: New scoped grant
grantForm.userIdHint: The id of the user account (User::<id>). A grant to an unknown id confers nothing.
grantForm.roleHint: A built-in role confers its standard permissions; a custom role confers its bundle.
grantForm.scopeClassHint: Optional. Narrows the grant to one resource kind (e.g. only models).
grantForm.noteHint: Optional context recorded with the grant.

defs.title: Custom roles
defs.caption: Reusable permission bundles defined for this organization. Built-in roles always remain; a custom role complements them.
defs.name: Name
defs.deleteBody: The role is removed. A role still referenced by a grant cannot be deleted — revoke the grant first.

roleForm.name: Name
roleForm.nameHint: Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore. Used in policy; the display name below is shown in the UI.
roleForm.permissionsHint: Pick the verb (read/write/admin) for each resource kind.
roleForm.groupsHint: The role also confers every permission of the groups you select.
roleForm.baseRoleHint: Start from a built-in role, resolved live: the role keeps meaning "everything this role has" as the catalog grows. Leave empty to list permissions explicitly.
roleForm.excludesHint: Subtracted after the base, the permissions above and every included group — so nothing can add them back. Excluding something the base does not grant today is valid: the exclusion still holds when it does.

groups.title: Permission-groups
groups.caption: Named bundles of permissions you can include in several custom roles.
groups.name: Name
groups.deleteBody: The group is removed. A group still included by a custom role cannot be deleted — remove it from the role first.

matrix.notDeclared: Not declared by any mounted module: {{perm}}

groupSubjects.title: Group subjects & hierarchy
groupSubjects.caption: Grant roles to provisioned user groups and shape the group hierarchy. A child group's members inherit the parent's grants.
groupSubjects.noGroups: No provisioned groups. Groups are pushed by the identity provider (SCIM).
groupSubjects.setParentBody: Members of {{child}} will inherit the grants of {{parent}}. The engine re-evaluates on the next request.
groupSubjects.clearParentBody: {{child}} will no longer inherit its parent's grants.
groupSubjects.cycleError: Cannot set parent: it would create a cycle.
groupSubjects.mapRoleBody_one: Every one of its {{count}} current member gains this role immediately, and anyone the directory adds later inherits it too.
groupSubjects.mapRoleBody_other: All {{count}} of its current members gain this role immediately, and anyone the directory adds later inherits it too.
groupSubjects.roleHint: Clearing the mapping only narrows access, so it never needs extra authority.
groupSubjects.roleCeiling: You cannot grant a role above your own rank. This is not a missing permission — ask someone more senior to make this mapping.

modelGroups.title: Model-groups
modelGroups.caption: Named sets of models. A model belongs to a group if it is listed explicitly, or matches a family or tier selector.
modelGroups.name: Name
modelGroups.memberRefsHint: One model ref per line (exact or prefix match).
modelGroups.familySelectorsHint: One model family per line (e.g. claude, gemini).
modelGroups.tierSelectorsHint: One access tier per line (e.g. free, standard, enterprise).
modelGroups.deleteBody: The group is removed. Model-access rules that reference it by name will no longer match.
modelGroups.truncatedHint: The engine reports more model groups than were loaded. A group missing here does not demonstrate that it does not exist — an access rule may still target it.

modelAccess.title: Model-access rules
modelAccess.caption: Who may (allow) or may not (forbid) use which model or model-group. A forbid overrides any matching allow.
modelAccess.deleteBody: The rule is removed and the engine re-evaluates model access on the next request.
modelAccess.subjectRefHint: The user id, role name, or agent-group slug.
modelAccess.targetRefHint: The model ref (exact or prefix) or model-group name.
modelAccess.effectHint: Allow grants access; forbid overrides any matching allow.
modelAccess.workspaceRefHint: Optional. Restricts the rule to one workspace (empty = tenant-wide).
modelAccess.surfacesHint: Optional. Restricts to specific integration surfaces (empty = all).
modelAccess.truncatedHint: The engine reports more access rules than were loaded. Read the rules with that in mind: allows that confine a subject and forbids that subtract access may both be missing, so this page can read wider OR narrower than reality. Do not infer effective access from it.

accessReview.title: Access review
accessReview.caption: Reverse queries: who can access what? The engine evaluates every candidate — results are authoritative, not cached.
accessReview.readOnlyNotice: You need authz read access to run access reviews.
accessReview.exportHint: Produces a sealed evidence pack for one resource — recorded in the tamper-evident audit ledger.
accessReview.resourceIdHint: The id of the resource, agent, or session.
accessReview.actionNameHint: The permission to check (e.g. agent:read, resource:write).
accessReview.subjectIdHint: The id of the user or token principal.
accessReview.loadError: Could not run the query. Try again.

activation.title: Business activation
activation.caption: Turn on the add-ons your edition includes. Controls with a safe default activate; controls that need a secret or a policy review are staged for you to fill and promote.
activation.unavailable: Activation is available in the business edition.
activation.restartNote: Activation applies at the next engine restart (add-ons are wired at boot).
activation.promoteHint: This add-on is staged and its configuration is ready. Activation applies at the next engine restart.
activation.enableHint: Review the changes below. Staged add-ons need input before they activate.

bindings.readOnlyNotice: You need source-scope binding access to view bindings.
bindings.title: Source bindings
bindings.caption: Bind a real source reference to workspaces, folders, agents, sessions, users, groups or roles. Credential fields are references only; the console never stores a value here.
bindings.sourceRefHint: Use the exact source ref. There is no single catalog for every source kind.
bindings.pickSourceHint: Choose a source type and enter its source reference to load bindings.
bindings.noneHint: Without enabled allow bindings, the source remains global unless forbidden subjects are present.
bindings.formCaption: The backend validates store-resident scopes. Subject refs are shape-validated and unknown refs match no actor.

ref.agentHint: Agents are selected by external id.
ref.sessionHint: Route-gated session axis. An unknown ref matches no session.
ref.userHint: Authenticated-principal axis. An unknown id matches no user.

bindings.credentialHint: Optional. If any credential field is set, name, kind and locator are required.
bindings.inlineCredentialError: Use a locator only. Do not paste URLs with credentials or token/password query parameters.
bindings.credentialIncomplete: A scoped credential needs a name, reference kind and locator.
bindings.credHintHelp: Short masked partial only, never a full credential.
bindings.credHintTooLong: The hint must be 64 characters or fewer.
bindings.noteTooLong: The note must be 512 characters or fewer.
bindings.queued: Relaxation queued — awaiting a second approver.
bindings.deleteBody: Deleting a forbid or the last enabled allow relaxes enforcement and will be queued for dual-control approval.
bindings.disableTitle: Disable all scoping for this source?
bindings.disableBody: This proposes disabling every enabled binding for the source. It is always queued for a second approver.
bindings.queuedBody: {{op}} for {{source}} is awaiting a second, distinct approver.

folderPicker.label: Resource tree
folderPicker.emptyHint: The folder picker only lists Resources returned by the source-scope resource endpoint.
folderPicker.truncated: This level is incomplete — the engine reports more nodes than were loaded. A resource you cannot see here cannot be chosen, and the id you pick becomes the anchor the engine enforces on.

preview.title: Resolution preview
preview.confined: {{source}} is confined because it has at least one enabled allow binding.
preview.globalWithForbids: {{source}} is global except for the enabled forbid bindings below.
preview.global: {{source}} is global because it has no enabled allow bindings and no enabled forbids.
preview.algebra: Forbid is absolute. When at least one allow binding is enabled, only matching subjects reach the source. Scoped credential precedence is session > agent > user > user_group > role > agent_group > folder > workspace.
preview.noEnabled: No enabled bindings participate in resolution.

actor.title: Per-actor verdict
actor.hint: Ask the engine what it would decide for one actor against this source.
actor.baseline: BASELINE only — the engine runs the real resolver with a zero principal, so this is the deny-closed floor. What this actor's own grants or RBAC would add is NOT simulated.
actor.empty: Enter an actor reference to ask the engine.

posture.title: Relaxation review queue
posture.caption: Relaxing source-scope enforcement is proposed by one operator and applied only when a second, distinct admin approves it.
posture.noneHint: Relaxing updates, deletes and disable-scoping requests appear here.

target.unknown: not resolved — the assignment list did not load in full
target.notApplicable: not an assignment target — this resolver does not apply

posture.truncatedHint: There are more posture requests than shown; this page takes rows by id and the status filter is applied by the ENGINE, so the cut is of the already-filtered queue — there are more requests inside it than these.

bindings.truncatedHint: There are more bindings for this source than shown; this page takes rows by id — assigned at creation — so later rows are missing. A binding not listed here does not demonstrate that the source has no such binding.
bindings.pickerTruncatedHint: The engine reports that more options exist than were loaded, so this picker is INCOMPLETE. If the one you need is not listed, that does not mean it does not exist — there is no server-side search here, so use the API for now. Choosing a different entity because the right one is not listed is how a binding ends up anchored to the wrong thing.

entitlement.title: What you have, what you are entitled to, and what is switched on
entitlement.description: Three independent questions with three different sources. The console composes them; it does not pick one.
entitlement.threeQuestions: These are three separate questions and two of the columns will often say "not known". That is the correct answer, not a loading failure: "no" is a claim about the product, "not known" is a claim about our ability to measure, and this is the worst screen in the product to confuse them in.
entitlement.noVerifiedLicense: ⛔ There is no verified licence, so the engine sends no attested feature claims at all. Entitlement is therefore NOT KNOWN for every add-on below — which is not the same as having none.
entitlement.binaryUnknownWhy: The edition ({{edition}}) is a property of the BINARY, not of a module: it is a function of the build tag and is exactly what a restart-free apply cannot change. The engine does not publish which modules a given binary compiled in, so per add-on this column is honestly not known. It is not inferred from the packaging tier, because a preset is packaging and a build tag is compilation, and they are not the same thing.
entitlement.noAddons: The engine publishes no add-on catalogue on this build, so there is nothing to compose. That is not the same as there being no add-ons: an older or community binary answers this endpoint with a 501.
